{{Quote|People love the X-wing pilots because they think of them as the great fighters of the Rebellion. See? People haven't forgotten the war. It's just that it was all so very long ago.|[[Senator]] [[Varish Vicly]]|<ref name="Bloodline" />}}
The '''T-65B X-wing starfighter''', also known as the '''T-65B space superiority fighter''', or '''T-65B X-wing multi-role starfighter''', was a single-seat craft manufactured by [[Incom Corporation]] and used most famously by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. Renowned for its speed and maneuverability during the [[Galactic Civil War]], it became the backbone of the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps]], being both harder hitting and tougher under fire than its main adversary, the mass-produced [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter]] of the [[Imperial Navy]].

[[Standard year|Years]] following the [[Galactic Concordance|destruction]] of the Galactic Empire and the [[Declaration of a New Republic|establishment]] of the [[New Republic]], the T-65B was initially retained by the [[New Republic Defense Fleet]] before eventually being replaced by newer X-wing models, such as the [[T-70 X-wing starfighter]], and the [[T-85 X-wing starfighter|T-85 X-wing]].

==Characteristics==
===Overview===
{{Quote|My first time out, I didn't know an S-foil from a nose cone.|"Red Three"|<ref name="Battlefront" />}}
[[File:T-65b_blueprints.png|thumb|left|200px|X-wing schematics]]
The T-65B X-wing [[starfighter]],<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> referred to as the T-65B space superiority fighter, or T-65B X-wing multi-role starfighter,<ref name="FFG SnS">''[[Starships and Speeders]]''</ref> was manufactured by [[Incom Corporation]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> It was designed to excel in all aspects of starfighter combat, being highly maneuverable and heavily shielded, with a small profile that made it harder to hit. Unlike other starfighters the X-wing could excel in atmospheric flight. This included outmaneuvering the TIE fighter, which was otherwise faster and more maneuverable than the X-wing in space.<ref name="RSOWM" /> The X-wing was classified as a starfighter,<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> specifically a [[snub-fighter]] due to its size.<ref name="ANH" /> The starship weighed 18,000 kg.<ref name="Absolutely">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''</ref>

It had two pairs of wing-like strike foils, or [[S-foils]], mounted at the rear of the craft on opposite sides. Normally, the foils on each side locked in place flush against each other; during combat, however, the foils were folded out. This gave the craft its distinctive "X"-like appearance when viewed from the front or rear. The S-foils were controlled by an [[S-foil servo actuator]] located in the back of the starfighter.<ref name="SWCT" /> With the S-foils open in attack position, the craft had a greater spread of fire as opposed to whilst shut.<ref name="youtube rebels recon">{{RebelsRecon|gapXiLIYifI|#4.6: Inside "Jedi Night" & "DUME" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/disneyxd-rebels-recon-inside-jedi-night-and-dume}}</ref>

[[File:Carson-in-Xwing.jpg|thumb|left|275px|Carson Teva in the cockpit of his T-65B X-wing]]
The [[cockpit]] had flight controls similar to those of the [[T-16 skyhopper]], an [[airspeeder]] also produced by Incom Corporation,<ref name="Encyc" /><ref name="RSOWM" /> along with a [[targeting computer]] with holographic imaging system.<ref name="RSOWM" /> Under the X-wing was a cargo compartment,<ref name="SWCT" /> a [[repulsorlift]], and three reinforced landing legs to protect the craft from rough landings and take-offs.<ref name="RSOWM" /> Painted stripes on the rear of the S-foils identified each craft.<ref name="Databank X-wing History" />

S-foils in attack position provided the X-wing with additional stabilizer surfaces during air travel. While listed with a maximum atmospheric speed of 1,050 kph,<ref name="RSOWM" /> the X-wing could otherwise fly at supersonic speeds.<ref name="RSOWM" /><ref name="Shadow Fall" /> Indeed, with the engines at maximum thrust an X-wing could travel so fast it would glow hot from atmospheric friction. Doing so put tremendous strain on the starfighter and the pilot themselves however: after just several minutes of maneuvering at these velocities, gradual system failures began and even the cannons themselves were at risk of melting from the heat.<ref name="Alphabet Squadron">[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']]</ref> When traveling high in a planet's upper atmosphere, an X-wing could achieve speeds fast enough to cause the pilot's head to swim and their vision to glitter.<ref name="Shadow Fall" />

===Weapons and defense===
The craft was armed with four [[Taim & Bak]] [[KX9 laser cannon|KX9]] [[laser cannon]]s, placed at the tip of each wing. The laser cannons could be fired singly, in alternating pairs or all at once. By default the convergence or "zero" point where the lasers would intersect was set 500 meters in front of the X-wing. Two [[Krupx Munitions|Krupx]] [[MG7 proton torpedo launcher|MG7]] [[proton torpedo]] launchers were located in grooves near the middle of the underside of the fuselage on either side of the T-65B.<ref name="RSOWM" />

[[File:XWingStarfighterCard-PuzzleAndDragons.png|thumb|left|300px|The T-65B was an incredibly effective starfighter.]]
A [[deflector shield generator]] located in the rear of the X-wing created a protective field which could be adjusted around the craft with the help of a [[Chempat]] [["Defender" deflector shield projector|"Defender"]] deflector shield projector.<ref name="SWCT" /><ref name="ANH" /> This included shield projectors along the leading edges of the S-foils which, when in attack position, helped to expand the protective field. A [[Bertriak]] [["Screamer" sensor jammer]] provided additional defense by scrambling the sensors of enemy starfighters and homing warheads.<ref name="RSOWM" /> The X-wing could also use its laser cannons to shoot down enemy missiles.<ref name="Shadow Fall">''[[Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]''</ref><ref name="Hunted">{{EASWYouTube|f2VmOqjV_7Q|"Hunted"|int=Hunted}}</ref>

The single [[pilot]] sat in an armored cockpit in the center of the fuselage protected by a [[transparisteel]] canopy.<ref name="SWCT" /><ref name="RSOWM" /> The canopy allowed for a wider view compared to that provided by a TIE fighter's, and was also designed to automatically polarize to protect the pilot from harmful light. Explosive charges were set to blast the canopy clear in the event the [[Guidenhauser]] [[ejector seat]] had to be used. Adjustable for use by most [[species]], the pressurized cockpit had enough life support for up to one week, and featured an [[Acceleration compensator|inertial compensator]] to protect the pilot from high-g accelerations.<ref name="RSOWM" />

===Systems===
Four [[4L4 fusial thrust engine|4L4 fusial thrust]] [[engine]]s were attached to the wings of the T-65B, next to the fuselage. Some X-wings were fitted with [[4j.4 fusial thrust engine]]s, which were virtually identical to the 4L4 models. These provided the X-wing with incredible maneuverability thanks to three factors: the use of differential thrust between the four engines to adjust trajectory; a high-mass electromagnetic gryoscope fitted to each engine for swinging through tight curves; and the ability to fire retro-thrust forward through the turbine nozzles. Infrared suppressors were used to conceal the hot exhaust.<ref name="RSOWM" />

The X-wing itself was powered by a [[Novaldex]] [[04-Z cryogenic power generator|04-Z cryogenic]] [[power generator]] located in the center of the ship.<ref name="SWCT" /> Cryogenic capacitors located in the S-foils stored additional power for the engines. Power couplings allowed for energy to be distributed and balanced between the various systems.<ref name="RSOWM" />

[[File:CrashLanding-Legacies.png|thumb|right|250px|A Rebel pilot works to remove her astromech, who would serve as the ship's navigational assistant, from her crashed X-wing.]]
The X-wing was equipped with a long-range<ref name="Databank X-wing History">{{Databank|x-wing-fighter-history-gallery|X-wing Fighter History Gallery}}</ref> [[hyperdrive]] system<ref name="ESB" /> consisting of four [[GBk-585 hyperdrive motivator]]s.<ref name="RSOWM" /> An [[astromech droid]] served as the X-wing's navigation system, plugging into a socket near the engines above and behind the cockpit. The droid assisted with calculations and could hold up to 10 [[hyperspace]] coordinates, as well as make repairs to the craft.<ref name="Ships of the Galaxy" /><ref name="RSOWM" /> It could readjust power levels between different systems multiple times per second to assist the pilot in a fight.<ref name="Shadow Fall" /> The droid was capable of assuming full control of the X-wing if necessary too, with or without a pilot. In an emergency a separator charge would launch the droid clear of the craft.<ref name="RSOWM" />

The T-65B's [[sensor]] systems were located inside the X-wing's nose cone. The sensor system, a [[Carbanti]] transceiver package, was made up of a [[Fabritech]] [[ANs-5d "lock track" full-spectrum transceiver]], a [[Melihat]] [["Multi Imager" dedicated energy receptor]], and a [[Tana Ire]] [[Electro-photo receptor]].<ref name="SWCT" /> These fed information directly to the targeting computer, which could track up to 1,000 sublight objects and acquire 20 targets. Additionally, a Fabritech [[K-blakan mini sensor]] scanned directly behind the X-wing to detect sensor sweeps and craft approaching from the rear.<ref name="RSOWM" />

==History==
===Origin===
{{Quote|Third, rebel leadership would expend whatever resources were required to obtain additional starfighter squadrons. These efforts would cost credits and lives, and the details must remain confidential for now. Nonetheless, our access to X-wing fighters in particular is testament to our success.|[[Mon Mothma]], "[[Short Notes on the History of the Rebel Alliance Navy]]"|<ref name="Rogue One novel">[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The T-65B X-wing starfighter was envisioned by its designers as a fighter with both the speed and power to take on Imperial [[Star Destroyer]]s, ultimately delivering on both promises.<ref name="ICS">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> It managed not only to become the backbone of the [[Rebel Alliance Starfighter Corps]], but incorporated lessons learned in assessing the performance of [[Clone Wars]]–era winged starfighters, such as the popular [[Clone Z-95 starfighter|Z-95 Headhunter]] and the powerful [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170 starfighter]].<ref name="Databank X-wing History" /><ref name="Before the Awakening">''[[Before the Awakening]]''</ref>

Ironically, the Incom Corporation had first designed the X-wing for use by the [[Imperial Navy]]. The [[Galactic Empire]] had asked for a new rugged, single-pilot starfighter to help fill out its ever-expanding fleet, to which Incom was obliged to fulfill. Taking inspiration from the Z-95 and ARC-170, Incom engineers created a prototype that combined aspects of the two earlier designs. After receiving Imperial approval, production began on the new X-wing line, only to be halted. Ostensibly the Empire had found new concerns with the starfighter which caused the stoppage. In truth Incom had been sidelined in favor of [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] and their (much cheaper) [[TIE series]] starfighter. Faced with a glut of expensive starfighters going unsold, Incom was more than pleased when agents of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] eventually contacted them about making use of the X-wing<ref name="RSOWM" /> through methods that remained confidential to the greater Alliance.<ref name="Rogue One novel" />

Rebel forces<ref name="DawnRebellion">''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> used the X-wing extensively during resistance efforts against the Galactic Empire.<ref name="RSOWM" /><ref name="Lost Stars">''[[Lost Stars]]''</ref> Among the first revolutionary leaders to see how useful the T-65 X-wing could be in rebel operations, [[Saw Gerrera]] of the [[Partisans]] secured eight T-65s through the violent [[raid on an Incom warehouse]] and deployed them as the [[Cavern Angels]].<ref name="DawnRebellion" /> The Alliance to Restore the Republic proper would recover information about the X-wing—specifically plans, data, and prototypes for the starfighter—via the [[rescue of Incom personnel]].<ref name="RRaRS">{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic, Rebel, and Resistance Starfighters}}</ref> While X-wing starfighters were initially in general use, they eventually became solely affiliated with, and a symbol of, the Rebellion.<ref name="RSOWM" /><ref name="Lost Stars" /> Constantly hiding from Imperial detection, the Rebellion cleverly resorted to building its T-65Bs in hidden drydocks and hangars, far from the prying eyes of Imperial spies.<ref name="ICS" />

===Galactic Civil War===
====Yavin-era conflict====
[[File:Battle_of_Yavin.png|thumb|left|300px|X-wing starfighters in the pivotal Battle of Yavin]]
Several T-65Bs were kept at the Alliance's hidden fortress on [[Yavin 4]]. X-wings were used alongside [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|Y-wings]] in the [[Battle of Scarif]], aiding the rebel fleet above the planet to help [[Rogue One]] steal the [[Death Star plans]]. During the [[Battle of Yavin]], [[Luke Skywalker]] was assigned to an [[Red Five (T-65B X-wing starfighter)|X-wing]] for the battle, the goal of which was to destroy the Empire's approaching [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]]. Although many of the X-wing pilots were killed, Skywalker was able to launch his proton torpedoes into the battlestation's exhaust port, causing a chain reaction and destroying it. [[Wedge Antilles]] was the only other X-wing pilot who survived.<ref name="ANH" />

Aside from the Rebel Alliance, the [[Partisans]], a loosely-affiliated group led by [[Saw Gerrera]], utilized the X-wings as well, although they were given extensive paint jobs matching their organization, with several of them being used by the [[Cavern Angels]], as well as [[Edrio]].<ref name="Saw's Renegades">{{FFGXW|set=Saw's Renegades Expansion Pack}}</ref>

Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, the mercenary [[Saponza]] and his [[Saponza's partner|partner]] were involved in training X-wing pilots. They used a specially-modified astromech droid in order to draw out [[womp rat]]s, and a team of 20 X-wings were deployed to test their skills.<ref name="Commander">''[[Star Wars: Commander]]''</ref> During the war, a contingent of the Alliance starfighter corps, including three X-wings, was [[Skirmish aboard Accresker Jail|dispatched]] under [[Tan Leader]] to the planet [[Tiferep Major]] to help with a planetary evacuation. Tan Leader themself piloted an X-wing, only for the pilot and their starfighter to be destroyed by [[Darth Vader's lightsaber]].<ref name="Aphra 25">[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 25|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 25]]</ref>

====The later war====
[[File:Xwingdockedinhangar.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An X-wing starfighter receiving repairs in Echo Base]]
The Alliance also brought X-wings to their new headquarters, [[Echo Base]] on [[Hoth]]. They were launched during the Empire's [[Battle of Hoth|invasion]] of the base to protect the escaping [[GR-75 medium transport|transports]].<ref name="ESB" /> Then-rookie pilot [[Adon Fox]] was the sole X-wing pilot assigned to protect his wife's transport, but it did not make it past the Imperial blockade.<ref name="Blade Squadron">{{InsiderCite|issue1=149|issue2=150|Blade Squadron (short story)}}</ref> After escaping, Skywalker avoided the rendezvous point to visit with [[Jedi Master]] [[Yoda]] on [[Dagobah]], who would [[Jedi Training|train]] him to become a [[Jedi]]. He then took his X-wing to [[Cloud City]] on [[Bespin]] to rescue his comrades.<ref name="ESB" />

Skywalker later recovered his X-wing from Bespin during a subsequent [[mission to Cloud City]].<ref name="Star Wars (2020) 4">[[Star Wars (2020) 4|''Star Wars'' (2020) 4]]</ref> For the climactic [[Battle of Endor]], the Rebel Alliance assembled their entire fleet for the assault on the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]]. X-wings were assigned to [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]] for the battle under the command of Wedge Antilles. Although several X-wings were destroyed, Antilles used his fighter to destroy the battle station's power regulator, contributing to its destruction.<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

X-wing fighters were also present at the [[Battle of Jakku]],<ref name="Battlefront" /> and at least one fighter was shot down during the battle and its wreckage was preserved at the [[desert]] surface for nearly thirty years.<ref name="Episode VII">{{Film|VII}}</ref>

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Compared to the Resistance's current T-70 X-Wing squadrons, these stats still hold up pretty well. I'm always happy to fly a T-65.|[[Resistance pilot]] [[Poe Dameron]] on the T-65's stats|<ref name="Star Wars: The Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>}}
In the years following the destruction of the Galactic Empire, newer X-wing models, such as the [[T-70 X-wing starfighter]] would eventually fall into the hands of the [[Resistance]], and the [[T-85 X-wing starfighter|T-85 X-wing]] would see use in the [[New Republic Defense Fleet]].<ref name="Before the Awakening" /> Despite the wide-spread retiring of T-65s in favor of newer models, Luke Skywalker, now a Jedi Master, continued to use Red Five as his main starship.<ref name="Episode VIII">{{Film|VIII}}</ref>

While training a [[Jedi Order|new generation of Jedi]], Skywalker lost his students when the [[dark side adept]] [[Snoke]] drew Skywalker's nephew, [[Ben Solo]] to the [[dark side of the Force]]. Becoming "Kylo Ren," Solo and the [[Knights of Ren]] killed all of Skywalker's students and burned his [[Jedi Temple of Luke Skywalker|Jedi temple]].<ref name="Episode VIII" /> In search of the [[First Jedi Temple]], Skywalker went into [[Exile (punishment)|exile]]<ref name="Episode VII" /> and traveled aboard his X-wing alone. After traveling to [[Ahch-To]], he purposely ditched his X-wing in a shallow inlet, leaving himself stranded on the [[Temple Island|island]], and cut himself from [[the Force]], until [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] came to be his final apprentice before dying and becoming one with the Force.<ref name="Episode VIII" />

Rey later purposely crash-landed [[Kylo Ren's TIE whisper]] on Ahch-To, wanting to do the same thing Luke did, but his [[Force spirit|spirit]] lifted his old X-wing out of the water for her to travel to [[Exegol]] and then return to the [[Resistance base (Ajan Kloss)|Resistance base]] on [[Ajan Kloss]] after the war [[Battle of Exegol|ended]].<ref name="Episode IX" />

==Behind the scenes==
The X-wing appears in the [[original trilogy]]. The sound for it was generated by a passing artillery shell. The concept art designed by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] for the X-Wing shows the two engines split into four smaller engines on each wing when S-foils are open. This design was later used for the [[Z-95 Headhunter]].

Originally, Red Squadron was going to be named [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]]. However, the limits of bluescreen technology in the late 1970s caused problems for the blue markings, so the squadron name and color was changed. The original designation was retained for [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|the ''A New Hope'' novelization]]. The first X-wing model was built in 1975 by [[Lorne Peterson]], [[Grant McCune]], and [[Steve Gawley]] as Blue One before the squadron name was changed. This model was later repainted as Red Two.<ref name="makmodeler">http://www.makmodeler.com/?p=951 {{C|link obsolete, redirects to an image of a snowspeeder on http://www.jasoneaton.com/Mystery10/p7280029-1}}</ref>

Several models, including both "hero" and "pyro" models (simpler casts taken from the "hero" X-wings and rigged to be blown up for effects shots) were built by ILM for the original film. Between the two types, at least eight of Red Squadron's X-wings were represented: Red One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, and Twelve have all been confirmed, with the eighth unidentified. Red Four and Six were pyro models destroyed during filming, while only the wings of Red Five have survived. The only model known to remain intact today is the hero model for Red Three, and the fates of the others are unknown.

Despite the number of models built, they were ultimately used in effects shots with little regards to continuity (such as Red One appearing in the trench with Red Five). When the effects teams on the Special Editions later created new footage for the Battle of Yavin using CGI, only two different sets of markings were recreated—those of Red Two and Five—and applied to all X-wings in the revised battle scenes.

For the ''[[Star Wars Anthology Series]]'' film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', the X-wings at the Rebel base were realized by a combination of full-size props and cutouts, similar to the fighters in the original ''Star Wars'' film.<ref name="Star Wars Archeology">{{SWYouTube|JUafi3EWBY8|Star Wars Archaeology Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}}</ref>

A new version of the X-wing, known as the T-70 X-wing starfighter, appears in [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']]. With its wings closed, the craft looks much closer to Ralph McQuarrie's original concept sketches than the effects models from the final films. However, the wings on this version scissor open along the span rather than split across the chord as in the original design, resulting in distinct forward and aft wings, with the forward lower wings being somewhat narrower in chord than the aft upper wings.

''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]'' stated that Luke Skywalker had salvaged an S-foil from the X-wing which he used as a door for his [[Luke's hut|hut]].<ref name="TLJ VD">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> This is apparently contradicted by [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']], which depicts his X-wing with its S-foils intact.<ref name="Episode IX" />
